blocks.text: Why Bilingual Nurses Are in High Demand in Canada

blocks.html:
Bilingual nurse jobs in Canada are growing — especially in Ontario and New Brunswick. Les infirmiers bilingues améliorent la sécurité, la confiance et la qualité des soins.

Hospitals and clinics need French-English nurses who can support diverse patients. Offrir des soins dans les deux langues officielles est maintenant une priorité dans de nombreux établissements de santé.

items.question: Do I need to be fluent in both languages?
items.answer: Yes. Proficiency in both French and English is required for bilingual-designated roles, including RN, LPN, NP, PSW, HCA, and allied health positions.

items.question: What provinces need bilingual nurses most?
items.answer: Ontario, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, and PEI consistently request bilingual staff. We also receive bilingual job orders from Manitoba and Alberta.

items.question: Are bilingual healthcare professionals paid more?
items.answer: Many facilities offer bilingual premiums or prioritize bilingual applicants for patient care roles where language is a key part of service delivery.

items.question: Do you hire bilingual HCAs, PSWs, or allied health professionals?
items.answer: In addition to bilingual nurses, we also place bilingual PSWs, HCAs, and allied health professionals in roles across Canada.

items.question: What if I’m only licensed in one province?
items.answer: We’ll help you transfer or obtain additional provincial licensure so you can access more opportunities.

items.question: Can I work in telehealth if I’m bilingual?
items.answer: Yes. We offer virtual care roles that require fluency in both languages for triage, patient assessments, and follow-ups.

blocks.html: Goodwill Staffing places bilingual nurses in healthcare roles across Canada. We support RNs, LPNs, and NPs fluent in French and English with licensing, housing, and job placement across provinces. From hospitals to telehealth, we make bilingual careers happen.
